item.text: {"question_id":"6B.8","answer":"During 2023, the Tshisekedi government enacted or maintained several relevant protections: Indigenous-rights legislation, conflict-related sexual-violence victim protections and reparations, gender-violence measures, and targeted plans for safer and more equitable girls’ education (BATCH-0001-E010; BATCH-0029-E002; BATCH-0011-E003; BATCH-0026-E009). UNDP-supported justice and police-reform activities also produced measurable outputs, including magistrate recruitment, legal-aid access, mobile-court judgments, police training, and a provincial criminal-analysis bureau, but these were substantially supported by UNDP and partners and do not establish Tshisekedi’s personal direction or nationwide remedy (BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0009-E005). Practical equality and dignity remained weak: discrimination against women, Indigenous peoples, ethnic minorities, disabled people, and LGBTQI+ people persisted; disability protections were poorly enforced, fewer than 1 percent of children with disabilities attended school, and election infrastructure remained inaccessible to many older and disabled voters (BATCH-0002-E022; BATCH-0011-E015; BATCH-0026-E010; BATCH-0026-E009; BATCH-0023-E002). Enforcement failures included rare or ineffective accountability for gender, disability, Indigenous, and LGBTQI+ abuses, limited access to remedies, and alleged abuses against Indigenous peoples and local communities during law-enforcement operations (BATCH-0011-E015; BATCH-0014-E005). State forces also restricted peaceful assembly and used serious violence, including the May protest abuses and the August Goma killings, while authorities’ subsequent investigations and convictions did not demonstrate comprehensive remedy (BATCH-0002-E012; BATCH-0011-E011; BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0025-E005). Mining-related evictions and abuses further showed inadequate consultation, compensation, grievance mechanisms, and redress, although the evidence does not prove the president personally directed those acts (BATCH-0010-E018).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E010","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E005","BATCH-0002-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E022","BATCH-0011-E015","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0002-E023","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0025-E005","BATCH-0010-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal laws and program outputs are better documented than enforcement, nationwide access, durable remedy, or group-level outcomes.","Several favorable measures were externally supported or government-reported, limiting inference about Tshisekedi’s personal causation.","Some adverse findings involve non-state actors, local authorities, security commands, or mining companies; presidential responsibility is therefore not established for each incident.","Some adverse evidence concerns conditions inherited from earlier years or conduct documented in 2023 but occurring earlier, limiting temporal inference.","The supplied evidence does not establish a complete national picture of accessibility, equal opportunity, or remedy across all protected groups."],"corrections_made":["Removed the overstatement that UNDP-supported justice outputs and police arrests directly demonstrated Tshisekedi-enacted and enforced remedies.","Added the omitted 2023 evidence on lethal protest suppression, ineffective disability and gender-protection enforcement, and alleged Indigenous and local-community abuses.","Separated formal commitments and selected implementation outputs from demonstrated practical equality, remedy, and nationwide enforcement.","Preserved uncertainty about presidential attribution for security-force and mining-related abuses."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
